source: AIDOC-catalogued Khmer farmer leaflet, "Coconut Cultivation Techniques for Farmers", prepared with NGO partners including Santi Sena, Buddhism for Development, and a farmer/agriculture association
text:
Good seed selection is presented as essential to a productive, healthy planting. Farmers are advised to select seed nuts from a mother palm that: has a straight trunk; is a known, true-to-type (non-hybrid) variety; shows no signs of disease; and has clearly visible varietal characteristics.

Within that, individual seed nuts should be chosen for full, well-developed water and flesh content (checked by weight/fullness), with clearly formed husk-fiber layers and a well-developed germination pore ("eye") end, since a poorly filled or immature nut is less likely to germinate reliably or produce a vigorous seedling. The leaflet illustrates this with cross-section diagrams of several coconuts, comparing the size and position of the internal water cavity and germinating embryo across different nuts as a visual guide to nut selection.
